market_holds: Spot 77.54 (sealed baseline, 2026-11-13 18:08 UTC), 52% below the 52-week high and 1.5% above the low; -5.3% over 5 sessions, -3.2% over 20. Front-expiry (11-20) straddle 7.28%, event-implied move 6.57% net of ordinary vol, 25d skew +1.2 vol points, put/call OI 0.62: no priced direction. Short interest about 3.6% of shares, 6 days to cover (FINRA 2026-10-30 via sweep row). The baseline's 6-K reaction history is not earnings (3-day cadence of HKEX buyback returns), so the real past prints come from Yahoo daily bars: Q3'25 (2025-11-18) opened -4.1% then closed +2.7%; Q4'25 (2026-02-26) opened -2.6%, closed -5.7%; Q1'26 (2026-05-18) opened +5.8%, closed +1.8%; Q2'26 (2026-08-18) opened -9.4%, closed -12.7% on an EPS miss and a qoq fall in AI revenue. Consensus as summarised in a 2026-11-03 Sina preview (10 days old, citing MS, BofA, UBS, Citi): Baidu Core revenue RMB 24.7-24.9bn (+1% yoy); online marketing about RMB 11.9bn, -22% to -24% yoy (UBS revised worse from -19%), which is about -9% qoq against Q2's 13.1bn; AI Cloud Infra +97% to +99% to about RMB 8.35bn (Citi), meaning a +14% qoq rebound from Q2's 7.3bn; core non-GAAP operating profit RMB 1.5-1.7bn (-25% to -31%; BofA cut from flat), with Citi flagging downside to profit consensus. Third-party EPS aggregates disagree ($0.57 / $1.05 / $1.72) and look stale. Sell side split: Citi, Daiwa, UBS, Nomura buy; Morgan Stanley Underweight with an $80 target (about spot). UBS notes market cap is below net cash and investments (RMB 283.1bn cash and investments at 2026-06-30). Known catalysts: first dividend promised for 2026 ('potentially by year-end' per the CFO in Feb), $5bn buyback through 2028, Kunlunxin spin-off.
view: This print turns on two lines that point opposite ways, and the street has set them that way on purpose. On ads, the line that sank Q2, the bar has been cut: consensus at about RMB 11.9bn needs a 9% qoq fall, against a seasonal Q2-to-Q3 dip of about 2-6% in 2024-2025. So an ad line merely in line with seasonality (around 12.3-12.6bn, -18% to -20% yoy) would read as 'decline stabilising'. On AI Cloud Infra, the line the bull case rests on, the bar is high and the line is lumpy. It went 8.8bn in Q1 (+79%) to 7.3bn in Q2 (+50%), a 17% qoq fall that drove the -8% qoq in AI-powered revenue behind the August sell-off. Consensus now wants 8.35bn, +14% qoq and about +99% yoy off a soft Q3'25 base. A cloud number in the 7.5-8bn range would look strong year on year and still miss. Profit expectations were already cut 25-31%, but depreciation and power costs are rising and Citi sees downside. Positioning is washed out (52-week low, below net cash, MS target at spot), and a first dividend could be declared with this print because the company said it would pay in 2026. Those two tilt the asymmetry slightly up. Persistent miss risk, a lumpy cloud line and the history of gap-downs (3 of the last 4 opens negative) tilt it back. I cannot rebuild either swing line from fresher data than the brokers had: no Q3 peer ad read-through exists before Monday (Tencent reports 11-18, Weibo 11-17), and I found no dated Q3 cloud contract or Apollo Go datapoint. Net: close to a coin flip with a slight upward lean, and nothing I would bet on.

recommendation.reason: The ad bar (-22% to -24% yoy, about -9% qoq) looks conservative against seasonality, and positioning is washed out at below-net-cash valuation, with a promised 2026 dividend as an option. But the cloud bar (+14% qoq after a 17% qoq fall in Q2) is high on a lumpy line, and profit risk is flagged by a bull. I could not show either side as mispriced with data the brokers lacked, so no mechanism clears the bar.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: AI Cloud Infra at or above about RMB 8.35bn with ads at or above RMB 12.3bn, plus a declared dividend, would make an up move likely. Cloud near Q2's RMB 7.3bn, or a large impairment like Q3'25's RMB 16.2bn, would make a down move likely.

self_critique: The case for a lean up: the ad bar needs a worse-than-seasonal quarter, the stock trades below net cash at a 52-week low with the main bear's target at spot, and a first dividend is promised for 2026, so a merely in-line quarter could squeeze 5-8%. The case for a lean down: the cloud line fell 17% qoq last quarter and consensus needs it to rebound 14%; Baidu has missed or gapped down at 3 of the last 4 opens; and depreciation and impairment risk sit on profit. Either case could be right. I hold 52 because I found no dated evidence that breaks the tie.
